- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during periods of sustained upward momentum; adjust upward by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- Overshoot after high true values (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at 5–10% below true peak.
- Lagged mean reversion: if true outcome is rising, forecast should not lag more than 2–3 days; adjust to align with 3–5 day moving average.
- Avoid overreacting to recent volatility — smooth out forecast spikes unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of divergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast variance if true outcome shows low volatility; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline.
